text:
linda-docs: Heads up — staging docsite build failed after the last docs PR. Linkcheck shows 404s for anchors when headings contain inline code and emojis, e.g. /guides#selecting-a-`model-name`-👍

oliver: I can reproduce locally with mkdocs. The slug generator turns the heading `Selecting a `model-name` 👍` into `selecting-a-model-name-%F0%9F%91%8D` (percent-encoded emoji) while the generated anchor in the HTML is `selecting-a-model-name-👍`. So linkcheck follows the percent-encoded version and fails.

maria: This smells like differing slug normalization between the markdown parser and the linkcheck step (maybe linkcheck sees the URL-encoded slug). Docusaurus/mkdocs variations handle emojis/wrapping ticks differently.

jon: Quick question — can we add explicit IDs to problematic headings as a stopgap? e.g.

```html
## Selecting a `model-name` 👍 {#select-model-name}
```

That should make both linkcheck and anchors stable until we fix slug normalization.

oliver: I tried that in a small branch and it fixes the staging error. But we have ~30 guides with backticked model names in headings. Might be tedious to patch all.

maria: Another option: update the slugify plugin settings in mkdocs/docusaurus config to remove emojis before slug generation (normalize to ASCII), or use a custom heading-id plugin that strips punctuation and emoji.

linda-docs: For now let's: 1) land the explicit-id patches for the pages referenced in the failing CI job, 2) open a follow-up issue to standardize slug generation across the site, and 3) add a CI rule that warns on headings with inline code + emoji combinations.

oliver: PR is opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/821 (patches 3 pages referenced by the CI log). Added a short note in the PR description about adding a slugify plugin ticket.

deploy-bot: CI: docs-linkcheck job failed on commit 9f3a2b7 — 3 broken anchors detected.

jon: I created issue #1023 with proposed slugify config and a couple of unit tests that mirror the reproduction. Assigning to @maria to pick up next sprint. :eyes:

maria: Taking it. I'll prototype a small slugify function that strips emoji and preserves backtick-wrapped code tokens as plain text (so `model-name` -> model-name). Will post patch for review by EOD tomorrow.

linda-docs: Thanks all — landing the hotfix now. If anyone sees other strange anchor encodings, drop them here and I'll triage. :thumbsup:
